chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man who hires an animal to a known place, so he exceeds it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The rent would be accounted for him in accordance with whatever he has exceeded with, and if the donkey is injured, so he would be responsible'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hiring an animal and exceeding the agreed destination?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of proportional compensation in Islamic contract law, where the hirer pays for the actual distance traveled rather than a flat fee, reflecting the Shia emphasis on fairness in commercial transactions. It further establishes the hirer's liability (daman) for accidental loss or injury to the animal during the unauthorized extension of the journey, a key concept in fiqh al-mu'amalat. This ruling underscores the Imam's role in detailing practical applications of general Quranic principles of justice and trustworthiness in daily economic life.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who hires an animal to a known place, so he exceeds it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The rent would be accounted for him in accordance with whatever he has exceeded with, and if the donkey is injured, so he would be resonsible’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al- Hassan al-Sayqal who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who hires a stumper to a certain place but he goes beyond such place. He (the Imam) said, ’He must pay for the extra distance; and if the donkey is destroyed, he is held responsible.’”
